comments.text: Architecture reference for this epic: use pingdotgg/t3code as the design baseline for provider layering. In particular, borrow the split between provider/session contracts and canonical runtime events (packages/contracts/src/provider.ts and providerRuntime.ts), plus the isolated Codex runtime manager pattern (apps/server/src/codexAppServerManager.ts), rather than threading Codex conditionals through the whole codebase.

title: Make provider selection a first-class concept

Model this after t3code's separation between provider contracts and runtime orchestration: provider kind/config/session metadata should be explicit, provider-specific runtime details should sit behind a clean factory boundary, and the rest of the app should depend on normalized provider state instead of raw CLI quirks. This includes config/types for selecting a provider, provider-aware session metadata in the DB, and a clean factory boundary so InstanceManager does not hard-code Claude SDK vs Claude CLI selection.
acceptance_criteria: Instances can declare a provider kind; provider choice persists in SQLite; InstanceManager creates sessions through a provider-aware factory; existing Claude behavior remains default-compatible; no UI behavior changes required beyond plumbing.

The adapter should support first-turn creation with codex exec --json, subsequent turns with codex exec resume --json, model overrides where supported, interruption/close semantics, and translation of Codex JSON events into relay output/activity/status messages. Scope is limited to sessions created and driven from the relay UI.

title: Integrate Skills support: display, install, and invoke via slash commands
description: Integrate Claude Code Skills into Relay. Display installed skills (likely from .claude.json — we may already have this via readClaudeConfig()), provide way to browse/install new skills from UI, allow /skillname invocation in the text input area. Consider autocomplete/suggestions when typing / in the input area.

comments.author: Eric
comments.text:
## Implementation Plan

### Goal
Display installed skills in the UI and allow /skill invocation via the slash command menu in the input area. Install/browse deferred to a future issue.

### How Skills Work on Disk
- Each skill is a directory with a required SKILL.md (YAML frontmatter + markdown body)
- Frontmatter: name, description (trigger text), optional version/metadata
- Optional extras: agents/openai.yaml (display name, icons), references/, scripts/, assets/
- No manifest — purely filesystem-based discovery. Symlinks used for sharing across scopes.

### Discovery Locations (priority order for dedup)
- Project: {projectDir}/.claude/skills/ (source: project)
- User (Claude): ~/.claude/skills/ (source: user)
- User (Codex): ~/.codex/skills/ (source: user)
- Agents: ~/.agents/skills/ (source: user)
- System (Codex): ~/.codex/skills/.system/ (source: system)

Project-level wins on name collisions. Global skills always included regardless of project context.

### Phase 1: Skill Discovery (server-side)
- New file: src/core/skills.ts with scanSkillDirectories(projectDir?) -> SkillInfo[]
- Reads SKILL.md frontmatter only (name, description) — not the full body
- Deduplicates by name (project > user > system)
- Add SkillInfo type to types.ts, extend ProjectArtifacts with skills field
- Wire into getProjectArtifacts() in instance-manager.ts

### Phase 2: Slash Menu Integration (UI)
- Pull skills from ProjectContext into use-composer-menus.tsx
- Merge into slashMenuItems with category Skill, grouped below built-in commands
- Selecting a skill inserts /skillname into the composer
- Invocation is pass-through: text sent as-is to Claude/Codex CLI

### Phase 3: Project Page / Skills Display
- Skills section on project overview page
- Card layout (ref: Codex App): name, truncated description, source badge
- No icons for v1 (skip openai.yaml parsing), generic skill icon
- No enable/disable toggle (read-only)
- Consider global Skills page accessible from sidebar

### Files Touched
- src/core/skills.ts (NEW)
- src/core/types.ts (add SkillInfo, extend ProjectArtifacts)
- src/core/index.ts (export)
- src/core/instance-manager.ts (wire into getProjectArtifacts)
- ui/.../use-composer-menus.tsx (merge skills into slash menu)
- ui/src/pages/project-page.tsx (skills display section)
- ui/src/context/project-context.tsx (expose skills)

### Deferred
- Install/browse/marketplace UI
- Full SKILL.md body reading
- agents/openai.yaml parsing (icons, display names)
- Enable/disable toggles
- MCP server display (separate concern)

Acceptance: restoreInstances should avoid eager transcript parsing for sidebar data; getHistory/subscribe path should hydrate external and managed sessions on demand; tests cover lazy restore metadata plus on-demand hydration; README and AGENTS.md reflect the new startup/hydration behavior.

comments.author: Eric
comments.text: Implemented lazy session hydration. Startup now restores DB-backed session skeletons only; sidebar/dashboard render from persisted metadata (title, last message preview, stats, git info); first history access hydrates transcript state and lazily boots managed provider sessions. Added schema v10 DB fields, updated restore docs, and covered the path with DB/history/websocket tests.

title: Introduce provider runtime bindings separate from Claude JSONL
description: Split managed-session runtime recovery from Claude transcript discovery. Persist provider-owned runtime binding data alongside generic session metadata, modeled after t3code's ProviderSessionDirectory/ProviderSessionRuntime: provider kind, resume state, runtime payload, and runtime mode should be recoverable without scanning ~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl. Claude JSONL parsing should remain a Claude-specific history/discovery mechanism, not the core managed-session source of truth. Acceptance: managed sessions can restore via persisted provider binding even if no Claude JSONL contract exists; InstanceManager no longer requires jsonlPath to persist managed sessions; Claude transcript watching remains supported as an optional/provider-specific path.

comments.author: Eric
comments.text: Added provider runtime bindings in SQLite via managed_sessions, including provider_name, provider_session_id, runtime_mode, resume_cursor_json, runtime_payload_json, and transcript_path. Managed instances now persist independently of Claude transcript discovery, while Claude JSONL remains an optional history/discovery read model.

title: Add plan mode toggle to text input area

title: Investigate session discovery for Claude Code IDE plugins (VS Code, Cursor, Zed)
description: Research how Claude Code's IDE plugins (VS Code, Cursor, Zed) store their session data — JSONL paths, project directory encoding, process names, etc. Currently the relay discovers CLI sessions via ps + lsof and reads JSONL from ~/.claude/projects/. IDE plugins may use different paths, process names, or session formats. Investigate: where do IDE plugin sessions write JSONL? Do they use the same ~/.claude/projects/ directory structure? Are the process names different (e.g. not 'claude' in ps output)? What changes are needed in discoverExisting/scanAllSessions to pick up IDE sessions? Goal: surface IDE plugin sessions in the relay UI the same way we surface terminal CLI sessions.

title: Audit token/cost tracking accuracy and add to Codex sessions

Acceptance: opening any session scrolls to the latest messages consistently; long virtualized histories with delayed measurement still settle at bottom; normal in-session scrolling behavior remains intact; tests added if practical; README/AGENTS updated if behavior/docs changed.

comments.author: Eric
comments.text: Updated ui/src/hooks/use-auto-scroll.ts so session-open scrolling stays pinned to the bottom through virtualizer/markdown remeasurement churn instead of relying on a single initial jump. The hook now runs a bounded settle-to-bottom loop after mount, ignores intermediate upward scroll adjustments during that forced settle window, and cancels immediately on explicit user intent (wheel/touch/pointer). Verified with npm run build:ui; repo lint warnings are pre-existing and unrelated.
